rv.q: Even uber-talented Bertie Carvel fails to enthrall as baddie Enrico.
The result remains, four centuries on, both easy to follow and hard to swallow.
Bijan Sheibani’s underpowered production proves unequal to the task.
The show has several not-quite-saving graces but it feels incoherent and underpowered...
Gate Theatre production of this canonical European text was for a fledgling Stephen Daldry , who brought an epic sensibility (and cast of 30) to a theatre seating not many more.

cn.t: This Spanish Golden Age drama about religion and redemption struggles to connect with modern audiences despite Bertie Carvel's performance, with critics finding the dated material alienating and the production a rare National Theatre misfire.
